svg.text: High-level architecture / source and runtime snapshot / 07 November 2026
LOCAL COMPUTER • Application + MySQL on host • Nginx and Redis inside Docker
Own clients, pool and cache cooldown
Own clients, pool and cache cooldown
Shared state lives in MySQL / Redis, not a port.
500 ms waiting deadline → MySQL fallback → 5 s process-local cooldown
Queue limit 100; offline queue disabled. Deadlines stop waiting, not the Redis command.
Each app creates a queue client.
V5 / STREAM ENTRIES ARE NOT THE PENDING LIST
ACK clears delivery tracking. It does not delete the original event from the stream.
Each click gets a new event_id.
Both boxes below are Redis-side data, not Node.js memory.
Not a second copy of event data.
On new delivery: Redis tracks the entry ID in the group PEL.
PEL = Pending Entries List. It tracks who still owes an ACK.
id ">": get entries not yet delivered to this group.
Loop: pending first, then new events
Same event retried -> no extra row
Restart as worker-1 -> read pending event -> duplicate event_id is safely ignored -> send ACK.
Database effect stays once. Redis pending record clears. Original stream entry remains.
Current limit: other consumers' pending entries are not reclaimed yet; permanently invalid events can retry indefinitely.
Blue / teal: data flow. Amber ACK arrow: removes pending tracking, never the stream entry. V5 remains in progress.
